subject: Hosted inference — intermittent soft-failures; automatic fallback active
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>

Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted inference — intermittent soft-failures; automatic fallback active

Hi team,

We wanted to let you know about an incident affecting a subset of hosted inference requests impacting some customers in the US region. Starting at ~09:55 PDT we observed a short wave of 'soft-failures' where some streaming generation requests either returned partial output or triggered an automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model variant.

What happened (TL;DR):
- Impact: ~2.3% of requests for certain long-context streaming calls experienced partial responses or switched to a fallback model for the duration of the wave.
- Mitigation: Automatic fallback routing to a compatible model variant was triggered to keep requests completing instead of failing. This reduced error rates but increased p95 latency for affected calls.
- Current status: Fallback remains active while our engineers complete validation; no additional customer-visible errors are expected beyond elevated latency on affected requests.

We're attaching a short graph showing the error vs fallback activation window (incident-graphs-20250612.png) and an interim timeline PDF with immediate actions taken. We'll post a short update to the public status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/20250612-hosted-fallback

Next steps we are doing now:
- SRE is investigating the root cause (initial signal points at KV-cache eviction cascade during a small eviction spike).
- We'll confirm when full routing back to primary model variants is complete and share a postmortem within 48 hours.
- If you'd like us to open a billing credit conversation, reply and I'll route to billing for a formal review.

Apologies for the disruption — I know reliability matters and we are treating this as high priority. I'll post a follow-up in ~30–60 minutes with more detail or earlier if anything changes.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai

Hi Jamie / Ava,

Quick technical update — thanks for the details, Jamie. We've been triaging in the SRE queue and here's what we have so far:

- Root cause (initial): a burst of KV-cache evictions on a narrow subset of GPU hosts caused increased cache misses for long-context streaming sessions. The cache miss pattern created transient latency spikes which pushed certain routing policies to trigger the fallback path that uses a smaller, compatible model variant. That path is designed to succeed rather than error, hence the higher p95 but lower failure count.
- Were payloads truncated: We observed several truncated/partial response events tied to the initial eviction window. Those were completed by fallback in most cases; a small fraction (~0.05% of total requests at the time) returned incomplete chunks that clients surfaced as truncation. We are collecting request ids and can share a list privately if you want to correlate with logs.
- Client changes required: No client-side changes necessary. Routing/fallback is handled server-side; when we route back to primary variants there is no API change.
- ETA: We expect to validate restoration and begin transitioning traffic back to primary variants within ~25–40 minutes from now (targeting ~11:05 PDT). We'll do a staged rollback with careful monitoring.

I'll follow up with a short packet of request ids and a proposed postmortem outline after we finish the initial rollback.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher | Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Hi Jamie — quick update: full service for the affected routing tier was validated and we began gradual traffic migration back to primary model variants at 11:05 PDT.

Summary of final state:
- Incident window: ~09:55–11:05 PDT (approx).
- Visible customer impact: elevated p95 for affected streaming calls during the window; a small number of truncated responses (~0.05% of total requests) were observed and logged.
- Recovery action: staged rollback from fallback routing to primaries after SRE validation; no client changes required.
- Next deliverable: 48-hour postmortem including timeline, root cause detail, and corrective actions (we will include a request id dump for cross-correlation).

If you'd like us to initiate an SLA credit review, let me know and I'll open a request with our billing team and provide a reference id. Otherwise I'll share the postmortem and the request-id list when it's ready.

Thanks for your patience — we'll keep improving our observability and routing safeguards to avoid recurrence.

Best,
Ava Chen
